paper.title: Achieving the Pareto Frontier of Regret Minimization and Best Arm Identification in Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandits, regret minimization with fixed horizon (sigma-sub-Gaussian rewards)
settings.definition_quote: Each item $i \in [L]$ is associated with a $\sigma$-SG reward distribution $\nu_i$, mean $w_i$, and variance $\sigma_i^2$... We focus on stochastic instances with a unique item having the highest mean reward, and assume that $w_1 > w_2 \ge \ldots \ge w_L$

settings.definition_quote: The algorithm $\pi$ aims to both minimize the pseudo-regret $R_T(\pi )$ and at the same time, to identify the optimal item with high probability, i.e., to minimize the failure probability $ e_T(\pi  ) := \Pr  (\iout^{\pi ,T} \ne 1 )$.

unmapped: joint objective: regret lower bound for algorithms whose fixed-budget BAI failure probability is at most exp(-phi_T)/4 on the whole class
settings.definition_quote: Let $\calB_1( \DeltaMin, \RMax  )$ denote the set of stochastic instances where (i) the minimal optimality gap $\Delta\ge \DeltaMin$; and (ii) there exists $R_0\in \bbR$ such that the rewards are bounded in $[R_0,R_0+\RMax]$. Let $\calB_2(\DeltaMin, \RMax ,\HtwoMax) $ denote the set of instances that (i) belong to $\calB_1(\DeltaMin, \RMax)$, and (ii) have hardness quantities $H_2\le \HtwoMax$.

settings.name_in_paper: Instances B_1' / B_2' with bounded variance (RM-BAI trade-off lower bound)

settings.definition_quote: Let $\calB_1'(\DeltaMin, \varMax )$ denote the set of instances where (i) the minimal optimality gap $\Delta\ge \DeltaMin $; (ii) for each item $i$, the variance $\sigma_i^2\le \varMax$.

settings.name_in_paper: Instances B_1(Delta,1): BAI failure probability / simple regret under a regret constraint

source.label: thm:rm_bd_lilUcb_para
source.quote: Let $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, $\beta\ge 0$, and $\gamma \in (0, \min\{ \log( \beta + 1+\varepsilon)/e ,1 \})$. For all $T\ge 1$, the pseudo-regret of {\sc BoBW-lil'UCB$(\gamma)$} satisfies R_T \le O( \sigma^2 \sum_{i\ne 1} \log(1/\gamma)/\Delta_{1,i} + 2TL\gamma^{1+\varepsilon} ), ...

results.notes: Paper's L = K. Proposition D.1 gives analogous bounds without the unique-optimal-arm assumption (with factor (1+eps)^3).

source.label: thm:rm_bd_lilUcb_para

results.notes: Paper writes T/L\gamma, interpreted as T/(L gamma).

source.label: thm:rm_bd_lilUcb_para
source.quote:
Furthermore, we can set  $\gamma = (\log T)/ {T}$ to obtain
\begin{align*}
    R_T

    \le O\bigg( \sigma^2    \cdot \sum_{i\ne 1} \frac{  \log T  }{  \Delta_{1,i}  }  \bigg)
    ,
    \quad
    R_T

    \le O \big(  \sigma^2    \sqrt{TL} \log  T     
    ~\big).
\end{align*}

source.label: thm:rm_bd_lilUcb_para
source.quote: Furthermore, we can set $\gamma = (\log T)/ {T}$ to obtain ... R_T \le O ( \sigma^2 \sqrt{TL} \log T ).

bound.regime: (T-L)/(1+eps)^3 >= sum_{i=1}^L 72 sigma^2/Delta_i^2 * log( (2.8/gamma^2) * log(11 sigma (1+eps)^2/Delta_i + beta) ), with Delta_i = max{Delta, Delta_{1,i}}; in particular when gamma >= gamma_1(Delta, H_2)

source.label: thm:bai_bd_lilUcb_para
source.quote: Let $\Delta_i = \max\{ \Delta, \Delta_{1,i} \}$ for all $i\in[L]$. For all $T\ge 1$, the failure probability of {\sc BoBW-lil'UCB$(\gamma)$} satisfies e_T \le \frac{ 2L(2+\varepsilon)}{ \varepsilon } ( \frac{ \gamma }{ \log(1+\varepsilon) } )^{1+\varepsilon}, if \frac{ T-L }{ (1+ \varepsilon )^3 } \ge \sum_{i=1}^L \frac{ 72 \sigma^2 }{ \Delta_{ i}^2 } \cdot \log ( \frac{2.8}{ \gamma^2 } \log ( \frac{ 11 \sigma (1+\varepsilon)^2 }{ \Delta_{ i} } + \beta ) ).

results.notes: Quantity is the failure probability e_T = P(i_out != 1).

tuning: gamma = gamma_1(Delta, H_2) = sqrt(2.8 log(6 sqrt(2.8) sigma (1+eps)^2/Delta + beta)) * exp(-(T-L)/(144 sigma^2 (1+eps)^3 (H_2 + Delta^-2)))

source.label: eq:lilUcb_bai_err_bd_best
source.quote: For all $T\ge 1$, when $\gamma $ assumes its lower bound $ \gamma_1(\Delta,H_2)$, we have e_T \le \tilde{O} ( L \exp ( - \frac{ T-L }{ 144 \sigma^2 (1+ \varepsilon )^2 (H_2 + \Delta^{-2}) } ) ).

results.notes: Paper's H_2 = sum 1/Delta_{1,i}^2 mapped to canonical H_1; paper's Delta (min gap) is Delta_min. Exponent has (1+eps)^2 in the statement although gamma_1 uses (1+eps)^3; recorded as stated.
